classification.summary: The customer wants to know how to hide members' street addresses on the members page while still showing their town so visitors can find them.
questions: How do I hide street addresses on the members page but still show the town?
How do I control which member profile fields are visible to visitors?

outputs.body:
Hi Mira,

Short answer: we can hide the street address, but the help center doesn't show a way to keep the town visible once it's hidden. We'll check whether there's a workaround and get back to you.

Here is what we know. To hide street addresses:

1. Go to Finance » Membership Plans and edit the plan the members are on.
2. On the Profile Page settings, set "Show Street Address" to NO.

The catch is that this setting also hides the location line in member search results. That is the city/state/country line, for example "Kansas City, Missouri, United States". So on its own it would hide the town too, which is not what you want.

Also, this is a plan-level setting. It applies to every member on that plan, not to individual members. The help center doesn't cover hiding the address for just a few members, so we'll look into that as well.

If the profile page also shows a map of the location, you can remove it on the same plan's Profile Page tab. Under "Select What Displays in the Overview Tab", set the Location Map position to "Hide Section".

Please don't change the address setting yet if you need the town to stay searchable. We'll write back within 2 business days with what we find.

The Lakeview team

evidence.question: How do I hide street addresses on the members page but still show the town?
evidence.answer:
The help center covers hiding the street address on public profiles, but it does not describe a way to keep showing the town once the address is hidden. Per the passages, turning the address off also hides the location line in search results.

1. Go to Finance » Membership Plans and edit the plan the members are on.
2. On the Profile Page settings, set "Show Street Address" to NO.

With this set to NO, the member's address no longer displays on their public profile. It also hides the location value in the member search results. The screenshot shows this is the city/state/country line, for example "Kansas City, Missouri, United States". So this setting alone will not keep the town visible.

If the member page also shows a Google Map of the location, you can remove it on the same plan's Profile Page tab. Under "Select What Displays in the Overview Tab", set the Location Map position to "Hide Section" (the screenshot shows this option).

evidence.question: How do I control which member profile fields are visible to visitors?
evidence.answer:
The help center passages cover page-level visibility (whole profile, contact, and review pages, plus search visibility) per membership plan, but not control over individual profile fields.

To restrict member profile pages for visitors who are not logged in:
1. Go to Finance > Membership Plans, select the plan, and click Edit.
2. Open the Search Visibility tab and use the Members-Only Access dropdown to tick Protect Profile Pages, Protect Contact Page, and/or Protect Write a Review Page.
3. Click Save Changes.

Things to know:
- The Members-Only Access setting is only available if the Members-Only Content add-on is active.
- If profile pages are protected but search results are visible to non-registered users, the phone number is also hidden from search results. Phone numbers are also hidden from search results for Inactive or Past Due members.
- The plan setting "Can Unregistered Visitors View These Members?" overrides the Members-Only Access settings. Setting it to "No" means users must be logged in to search for members in that plan. This is part of the Hidden Member Profiles add-on, available with the VIP Add-Ons Club or purchased individually.
- If a custom widget blocks the setting, the dropdown shows as DISABLED and the system displays the widget's name.

evidence.question: How do I change my profile photo on the mobile app?
evidence.answer:
The help center does not describe a mobile app, but it does explain how to change your profile photo from the Update Profile page in the account dashboard.

1. Open the account dashboard and go to Update Profile in the left Account menu.
2. If no photo is set yet, click Upload photo. If one is already set, click Change photo.
3. Choose a JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP image up to 5MB.
4. The image is cropped to a square and saved as soon as it uploads, so you don't need to click Save Changes for the photo.

To delete the current photo instead, click Remove.

evidence.question: Does uploading a new profile photo delete the old one?
evidence.answer:
Uploading a new photo replaces the old one on the profile; for the admin account photo you can also delete it outright with Remove, but the passages don't say whether the old file is permanently erased from storage.

- Admin account photo (Account Dashboard >> Update Profile): once a photo is set, "Change photo" replaces it and "Remove" deletes it. The new photo saves as soon as it uploads (passage 2).
- Member photos via the Users API: re-importing a profile_photo replaces the one on the profile straight away. Each import is saved under a new unique file name, so browsers and CDNs show the new picture instead of a cached copy. You don't need to remove the old image first. To delete a photo outright, use images_action = remove_profile_image (passage 6).

evidence.question: What should I do if my Brilliant Directories site shows a blank page?
evidence.answer:
The help center explains why a page may show blank, but it does not give troubleshooting steps to fix it.

What the passages say:
1. A blank page can mean a form on that page is missing. The example given is the "Website - Contact Us" form: when it is missing, regular users see no error, and the page simply shows blank.
2. Logging in as a website admin shows more information. For widget errors, admins see the widget name and/or the PHP error, which helps identify the cause. The screenshot shows an example: a red "Widget Fatal Error" box naming the widget and the PHP syntax error.

evidence.question: How can I check whether my site is down or whether there is a hosting outage?
evidence.answer:
You can run the built-in site checks under Settings > Domain Manager > Diagnostics, and you can recognise outage-type problems by the error screen visitors see, but the help center does not describe a way to check overall hosting/network status.

1. Open Settings > Domain Manager > Diagnostics (you need permission to view website resources).
2. Find "Is anything on this website broken?" and click Check everything.
3. Wait for the results and expand the details for any finding. The checks cover website launch status, purchased items awaiting installation, certificate problems and pending updates. Review the Domain and SSL findings first so an address or certificate problem isn't mistaken for a pending update. This is not a full audit of every custom page or integration.

Interpreting error screens:
- "Looks like there is a temporary issue connecting to the cloud": this appears when a server has a connection issue or heavy traffic. It is temporary, and the page reloads automatically within 60 seconds.
- "This website is offline and is no longer accessible": the site has been disconnected from the software. This can happen if the account is very past due or a shutdown was requested. If you think it's a mistake, contact support@brilliantdirectories.com or submit a ticket.

If the public site stays affected, contact support with the site ID, domain, the exact result and what you've already tried.

evidence.question: What should I do if payments fail at checkout on my Brilliant Directories site?
evidence.answer:
When a paid signup payment fails, the visitor sees the gateway's error and can correct their card details and resubmit; as admin, check the failure reason in the Activity Tracker or the notification email and reach out to the member to help.

What happens on a failed payment:
- The payment gateway rejects the card and an error message showing the gateway response appears (the screenshot shows e.g. "Your card was declined."). The visitor can update their card information and submit again.
- The member account is not created until payment is completed.
- The system emails the failed signup details to the Default Website Email (paid signups only; no notification for free signups).

What to do:
1. Go to Dashboard » Activity Tracker.
2. Open the Filters section and filter by "Finance".
3. Look for entries with the category "Failed Transaction". The description shows the name on the card, email, membership plan, billing cycle and address.
4. Read the 'Failed Signup Reason' at the bottom, which shows the exact reason the payment failed (the screenshot shows the error message and decline code).
5. Contact the member by email to offer help with completing the signup.

If payments aren't working at all, confirm a supported payment gateway is connected under Finance » Payment Settings.

sources.title: Finance » Payment Settings - Setting Up A Payment Gateway

evidence.question: How do I test the checkout and payment setup in Brilliant Directories?
evidence.answer:
Make sure a payment gateway is Active under Finance » Payment Settings, then run a test paid signup as a member; test purchases can be refunded and won't affect site revenue.

1. Go to Finance » Payment Settings and confirm a gateway shows "Active". If none is active, add one from the Supported Payment Gateways.
2. New sites on a directoryup.com subdomain already have test-mode payment credentials active, so you can test paid signups without adding a gateway. Transactions made with these built-in BD test Stripe credentials show a "Test Transaction" label in the transaction history. This label does not apply to custom Stripe accounts in test mode. These test credentials stop working once the site moves to a real domain, and you will then need a live gateway.
3. If you use your own Stripe account in test mode, real cards will not work. Use Stripe test card numbers (https://stripe.com/docs/testing) with any future expiration date and any CVC. For other billing countries, use Stripe's international test cards.
4. For PayFast:
   a. Select PayFast under Finance >> Payment Settings.
   b. Enter the sandbox Merchant ID and Merchant Key, set Enable Test Mode to Yes, and save.
   c. Register a member through the standard signup. The member should be redirected to PayFast; if not auto-logged in, use the sandbox Buyer Email and Buyer Pass.
   d. After paying, the member should return to your site and see a success confirmation.
5. When testing is done, switch to live credentials. For PayFast, replace the sandbox credentials with live ones and set Enable Test Mode to No.

evidence.question: What are the Brilliant Directories plan prices and add-on fees?
evidence.answer:
The help center passages do not list Brilliant Directories plan prices; they point to the pricing page instead. The only fee amounts stated are:

1. Website plans and pricing: see the Compare Pricing Plans page at https://www.brilliantdirectories.com/online-directory-pricing. The New Website button in the Account Dashboard also leads there. For more information, call +1 (800) 771-9332.
2. Clone My Website: you need an additional, unused website plan, and one of your sites is cloned to it. No separate fee is stated.

evidence.question: What is the refund policy for monthly payments?

What the passages do say:

2. Refund limits are set by the payment gateway. Some gateways don't allow refunds at all, some don't allow them through third-party sites like the BD admin, and some (such as Authorize.net) require at least 24 hours before a refund can be issued.

evidence.question: How do I import members or profiles from a spreadsheet in Brilliant Directories?
evidence.answer:
Prepare the CSV import template, then upload it via Search Members >> List Actions >> Import Members via CSV File (also reachable via Members >> Import Members >> Import CSV File).

Prepare the file:
1. Download a CSV import template. Row 1 holds the required headers; do not change their spelling or the import will fail.
2. Read the explanations in rows 2 to 4, then delete those rows. If you leave them in, they will be imported as members. listing_type accepts only Company or Individual.
3. Enter the member data in the correct columns. Delete any empty columns to make the file smaller and the import faster.
4. Optional: for images, put image URLs in the logo, profile_photo and cover_photo columns. Supported formats are webp, jpg/jpeg, png and gif.

Import the file:
1. Go to Search Members, open List Actions and select Import Members via CSV File.
2. Choose the membership plan under Assign Membership Plan. This is required.
3. Choose Set as ACTIVE Members or Set as NOT ACTIVE Members.
4. Optional: edit the auto-filled member tag (the import date and time) and pick a Tag Group.
5. Optional: under Advanced Options, choose to pass unique email checks or to create new categories from the file.
6. Click Browse to select the CSV, then click Begin File Import.

After the import:
1. If you included image URLs, go to Members >> Member Images.
2. Pick a results-per-page number and click Update Results.
3. Select all rows, choose Fetch from Source and Resize Photos, and click Apply Action. Do not leave the page while it runs.
4. Repeat for each page until all images are fetched.

On a directoryup.com test subdomain, add your own Google Maps API key before importing members with addresses.

evidence.question: Can a Brilliant Directories site display multiple languages?
evidence.answer:
Yes. For multi-lingual websites, the help center recommends the Google Website Translator add-on, which adds a "Select Language" dropdown to the site header so visitors can switch between languages.

To enable it:
1. Go to Settings » Design Settings » General » Header Design.
2. Set "Display Translation Tool" to "Yes - Display Google Translate" and save changes.
3. A "Select Language" dropdown will then appear in the site header. Visitors can return to the original language with the "Show original" button at the top of the page.

Notes:
- The site's default language won't appear in the dropdown, because it is the main language and doesn't need translating.
- Separately, you can set a single default language under Settings » General Settings » Localization » Default Website Language. If "Use same language for text labels and email templates" is checked and the language is on the supported list, text labels and email templates are translated automatically.
- Changing the default language does not translate everything. Header and main menus, for example, must be translated manually in the Menu Manager.
- For right-to-left languages, set the Advanced Setting "Text Direction" (text_direction) to "Right to Left".

evidence.question: Do old profile URLs keep working after a Brilliant Directories site move?
evidence.answer:
Not automatically: changing the website's domain does not, by itself, create redirects from every old address, so old-domain redirects need to be planned separately.

What the help center says:
1. Before switching domains, plan old-domain redirects separately. Changing the website address does not on its own establish a redirect from every old address (passage 5).
2. After the change, test the old-domain redirects along with the other site functions. DNS and certificate updates can take time to show everywhere (passage 2).
3. Within the site, the system automatically creates 301 redirects when member profile details change, such as URL structure, business name or address, so existing profile links still resolve (passages 1 and 4).
4. Redirects are added, edited, tested and deleted on the 301 Redirect Rules page (passage 1). They can also be managed through the API's redirect_301 model (passage 6).

evidence.question: How can I set up redirects from old profile links to new profile links?
evidence.answer:
In most cases you don't need to do anything: the system automatically creates 301 redirects from old profile links to new ones when member profile details change (URL structure, business name or address), including when the profile URL is changed through the API. You can also add redirects manually.

Automatic redirects:
- Changes made in the admin panel to profile URL structure, business name or address automatically create redirects, so existing links keep pointing to the updated profile.
- Changes made with PUT /api/v2/user/update also create a 301 redirect by default. To skip it for a single request, include create_301_redirect=0. This applies only to that request.

To add a redirect manually on the 301 Redirect Rules page:
1. Click New Redirect Rule.
2. In Source URL, enter the old profile path without the domain or a leading slash (EG united-states/los-angeles/top-level-category/sample-member).
3. In Destination URL, enter the new profile path.
4. To add more redirects at once, click Add Another Redirect and fill in the new row.
5. Click Save.

The Source URL is refused if it starts with http, www. or a slash, or if it matches the Destination. Quotes, angle brackets and backslashes are not accepted in either field.

For many redirects, such as after a migration, the platform also supports bulk import of redirect rules from a CSV file.

evidence.question: What should I do if password reset emails go to an address that is no longer in use?
evidence.answer:
The passages don't describe a direct fix for reset emails going to a dead address, but for members the reset email goes to the email on their profile, so an admin can update that email so future reset emails reach a working inbox.

1. Open the member in the Quick Edit module and update the Email Address field to the member's current address.
2. Note that this email is also the member's login username, so changing it changes the credentials they log in with. Tell the member about the change.
3. The member can then go to /login/retrieval, enter the new email, click "Get My Password", and follow the reset link in the email to set a new password.

outputs.body:
Hi Theo,

Glad the new members page is easier to read. Thanks for telling us.

We've logged your idea about saving a search so you don't have to pick the same town each visit. I can't say whether or when it will be built, but it is on record with the team.

No reply needed. If you think of anything else, just send it over.

The Lakeview team
